item.title: Illinois data centre project: $18 billion campus gets first permit as neighbours say they learned about it too late
item.description: Grayslake has granted a building permit for a substantial data-centre campus, representing a major advancement in an $18 billion private investment endeavor. Meanwhile, community members are voicing worries about lack of input and possible environmental repercussions. The developer is committed to thorough community engagement and meeting regulatory guidelines. Site work will be executed in phases, with initial construction about to kick off shortly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: MIT robot builds working laser cavity in 50 maneuvers under 30 minutes, self-corrects after disruption
item.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology researchers developed a robotic optics laboratory. This system autonomously assembles and aligns laser cavities with precision. The robot can also correct experimental setups after they are disturbed. This technology could accelerate testing for various optical devices and materials. Future applications envision remote interaction with these automated research environments.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 1927, Henry Ford built a town over a stretch of Amazon rainforest; in 1945 he was forced to sell it for $250,000
item.description: Henry Ford initiated the Fordlandia project in the lush Amazon rainforest of Brazil to secure a steady rubber supply. However, his corporate methods often clashed with local traditions and agricultural practices. The plantation faced numerous obstacles, including pests and diseases harming the rubber trees. Despite investing heavily over seventeen years, Fordlandia ultimately succumbed to failure, illustrating the challenges of integrating foreign business models within local ecosystems.

item.title: California buried a gas pipeline and removed its final barrier; salmon returned after 70 years
item.description: A decades-long barrier blocking fish migration in Alameda Creek was removed in 2025. This action reopened over twenty miles of upstream habitat for migratory fish. Chinook salmon were documented in the newly accessible area shortly after the construction. This marked the first access to this watershed section since the 1950s. The project is part of a larger, nearly thirty-year restoration effort.

item.title: Malibu Estate Price Swings: Carson’s former home jumps to $110m; sale history charts luxury surge
item.description: Johnny Carson's iconic Malibu estate has embarked on quite a price adventure. Initially acquired for around nine point five million dollars, the property was later listed at eighty-one point five million dollars. It ultimately sold for forty million dollars in 2019 and has now returned to the market, boasting a staggering price tag of one hundred ten million dollars.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1998, Alaska miner found a 294.1-ounce gold nugget; 23 years later, it sold for $750,000
item.description: In Alaska, a miner's incredible find of a massive gold and quartz specimen led to the unveiling of the largest gold nugget ever discovered in the state. Weighing over twenty pounds, this extraordinary piece, known as the Alaska Centennial Nugget, was held in a private collection until it hit the auction block in 2021, where it fetched an impressive $750,000.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California to open 2,060 coastal acres near Diablo Canyon as trails and campsites after $42m deal
item.description: A 2,060-acre stretch of California’s Central Coast near the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant will become a nature preserve after a $42 million conservation deal. The Wildlands Conservancy plans to open Wild Cherry Canyon to the public with hiking trails and campsites while protecting Native American cultural sites. The preserve is expected to open within five years, with guided tours possibly starting next year.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Swedish company is transforming discarded wind turbines into tiny-solar powered homes and recycled skis
item.description: The challenge of decommissioned wind turbine blades is becoming increasingly prominent in Europe. The composite materials used in these blades are notoriously difficult to recycle, leading to significant landfill concerns. In response, various companies are working on inventive reuse projects that could transform these retired assets into valuable materials, underscoring the necessity for a regulatory structure that supports sustainable initiatives in this industry.

item.title: Georgia city moves pre-Civil War house for hotel; $500,000 restoration turns it into coffee shop
item.description: After a careful relocation and restoration, the historic McCray House in Acworth, Georgia, is gearing up to welcome visitors as the new Bizarre Coffee shop. The city has committed nearly half a million dollars to preserve this pre-Civil War building, ensuring it continues to be a vibrant part of the community. As the coffee shop prepares to launch, it promises to inspire fresh memories in the heart of town.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Treated on floor, verandah’: Dhaka hospitals struggle as dengue wards overflow
item.description: Dengue cases are severely straining Dhaka hospitals, with patients treated on floors and verandas. Over 747 new patients were admitted nationwide in a single 24-hour period. August saw the worst dengue outbreak this year, reporting over 20,000 infections. Experts predict the situation could worsen further in October, requiring more action. Destroying mosquito breeding grounds remains the long-term effective solution.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Fourteen tail vertebrae found in Spain replaces North America as the only Diplodocus site
item.description: A significant paleontological breakthrough has occurred in Spain, where researchers have identified the first confirmed Diplodocus fossils beyond North America. Found in Teruel, these tail vertebrae date back around 150 million years. The discovery implies that during the Late Jurassic era, declining sea levels could have permitted dinosaurs to migrate between continents.
